segments.he: עַד שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם יַעֲמִיד פַּרְנָס. וּפַרְנָס לָאו שְׁלִיחוּתֵיהּ קָא עָבֵיד? אָמַר רַב הוּנָא, בְּאוֹמֵר: ״כׇּל הַזָּן אֵינוֹ מַפְסִיד״.
segments.en: § The mishna states that if his vow will remain in effect for «up to thirty days he must appoint a trustee» to provide sustenance to his wife. The Gemara is puzzled by this ruling: «And does a trustee not perform» the husband’s «agency?» If through his vow he has rendered it prohibited for her to derive benefit from him, how can he provide for her through the trustee? An action performed by an agent is considered to have been performed by the principal. «Rav Huna said:» The trustee discussed in the mishna was not actually appointed as an agent. Rather, the mishna is referring «to one who says» in general terms: «Whoever sustains» my wife «will not lose out.» Thus, anyone who complies does so of his own choice, although the husband will later compensate him. Therefore, the wife is not benefiting directly from the husband.
